correctness.rationale: The conditional Gaussian variance mixture with variance 2D/3 times the sum of cubed Poisson spacings is exact. The first-renewal transform gives the cited finite-time moment formulas. Differentiating the standardized fourth moment gives an explicit exponential polynomial H. Its Taylor coefficients vanish up to degree eight, are positive for degrees 9-15, and negative for all degrees 16 and higher, with the infinite tail controlled analytically by a closed falling-factorial formula. Thus H/z^15 is strictly decreasing with opposite endpoint signs, proving one and only one positive critical point; the strictly positive conditional variance proves excess kurtosis is positive. Symbolic inversion, expansion, and 70-digit diagnostics were run from check.py. No finite sample is taken as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The fourth standardized moment is a natural, experimentally measurable departure from Gaussian diffusion. Its strict global unimodality excludes every additional burst of transient non-Gaussianity and determines an exact parameter-independent peak amplitude and reset-rate-scaled peak time; the all-order transcendental sign argument is more than routine differentiation of the known moments. It is a complete structural classification for a physically motivated process, without claiming finite-sample performance or a general theorem for arbitrary renewal clocks.
